questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.answer: A town that I could see myself live in.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not easy. A lot of the information was in Portugiese. And I was almost daily at the international office.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: the international office was very helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: We had an intro meeting, but it was hard figuring out when the meeting was. I went to the university a couple of days before to ask, because I got no email with invitation.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A tough process, of finding classes in a portugese website, with TP's and different ways of doing things that we needed to be introduced to propperly. and afterwards, we needed to have all classes registred by signing from the professors.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The day the registration was, made no sense. All erasmus student camped outside the international office, in order to get help, due to it all being in portugese and all kinds of different forms, that we were not introduced to.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: international office

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: i ended up getting the classes i wanted, but only due to persisstance, and persuasion, to the professors, that all these classes was already on my OLA.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just give up, and go to the international office

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was not able to take IT subjects.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: it was very different from classes to classes. Some was the same level as denmark, some was less, some was above.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Veeeeerryy different. It was almost like returning to public school. Very interactive. The professors may call out your name, to read something outloud or point at you to answer a question. 
Also it was very much talking. Not so much theoretical stuff, or visuals to supply.

Live in the center of the town 
Take classes that align for a greater scheme 
Go to the international office of the day for choosing subjects, the webside is quite impossible.
